newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - Data to help gilts outperform.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - Data to help gilts outperform.

text.p: Domestic economic factors will take centre-stage this week as Britain's gilt market emerges from last week's dominant U.S. influence. Key inflation and employment news will keep market players on edge, but economists say the end result will show gilts continuing their recent outperformance of core European debt, cheered by signs of a slowdown in the British economic recovery.
"There is not a great deal to worry the market this week," John Shepperd, chief economist at Yamaichi International in London, told Reuters Financial Television.
"But there will clearly be some interest in the inflation report and in how hawkish the Bank of England wants to be about interest rates."

The Bank will release its quarterly inflation report on Wednesday and some analysts expect it to include a call for a 50 basis point rise in base rates to prevent price pressures from picking up. Base rates are now 6.0 percent. Bank governor Eddie George is expected to take a tough line on inflation, fearful that it is in danger of picking up pace in the longer term.

But analysts said recent subdued price numbers, including a fall to 10-year lows in January output prices announced on Monday, would ensure rate concerns were kept to a minimum among gilt market players.

Brian Hilliard, chief fixed income economist at Societe Generale, said underlying inflation data on Thursday, forecast to fall to 3.0 percent in January from 3.1 percent previously, would lend further support to an already healthy gilt market.
Yamaichi's Shepperd said Thursday's data might show a slight tick up in the annual rate of underlying inflation, but added: "I don't think that will make a large amount of difference to the market."
On jobs, analysts said gilts were prepared for another substantial fall in unemployment when figures are released on Wednesday.

But with a slightly less hefty decline expected than in December, when joblessness fell by 45,000, markets will be relieved to see a slowdown in job creation which should dampen economic activity in the first quarter of 1997.

The Reuters consensus forecast is for a 30,000 decline in unemployment in January. Confirmation that price pressures are under control and that the economy, while reasonably lively, is not threatening to bubble over, will prompt the spread to 10-year gilts over Bunds to tighten, adding to last week' impressive gilt performance.
But the spread, which has narrowed to 165 basis points from 182 in the last five sessions, is likely to shrink at a slower rate this week, analysts said.
"The spread should hit 160 basis points soon," said SocGen's Hilliard. "The mood is quite bullish, especially against the background of a very bullish Bund market and a reasonable Treasury market."
Analysts added that with an election approaching, volatility would creep into benchmark 10-year bonds in the near term.
Analysts at Merrill Lynch in London suggest a butterfly trade across the gilt curve could reduce the risk of any setback in 10-year paper while maintaining exposure to gilts.
They recommended selling 10-year gilts and buying into three- and 20-year paper.
